findings.title: Blanket Python healthy-pattern rewrites can widen strict contracts
findings.finding: The review rubric recommends isTrue/isFalse→truthiness and treats isinstance as an exact-type substitute elsewhere. Strict admission of True differs from admitting1 or a nonempty false string; exact numeric validation may intentionally exclude arbitrary subclasses as well as bool. Detector-zero is not behavioral equivalence or unique repair.
findings.recommended_action: Make semantic carrier/contract preservation a precondition of each rewrite and test wrong-type cases; keep syntax/style diagnostics separate from correctness.
findings.validation: CHECK-072 shows the accepted input set changes.

findings.title: Anti-mock snippet cannot justify its own clean-scan claim
findings.finding: Embedded scanner only finds ImportFrom nodes with module unittest.mock. It does not implement the advertised facade, tautology, monkeypatch, alias-import or Rust analysis, yet claims a clean scan supports their absence.
findings.recommended_action: Report exact predicates/language/population and implement separately tested rules before broad absence claims.
findings.validation: Full body review; no retained owner invocation.

findings.title: Paper-reader speed and fixture metrics are presented as broad verification
findings.finding: Mandatory1-to-1 mapping between each claim and Python/test/notebook/Lean ignores many-to-many and noncomputational claims. Absolute1e-12 numerical agreement and finite parameter stress tests do not certify prose theorems. Report template hardcodes100 percent and sustained-and-verified language without evidence binding.
findings.recommended_action: Separate usability timing, mapping completeness, finite checks and formal proof. Compute each actual denominator/status and bind artifacts, premises and checker results; use relations rather than forced bijections.
findings.validation: Full body review; no retained owner invocation.

findings.title: Scanner mode combination silently disables both rule families
findings.finding: CLI permits --arch-only and --pitfalls-only simultaneously; project sets AST rules empty and skips architecture pass. Parseable bad source then receives no active-rule findings, and console says codebase satisfies active rules.
findings.recommended_action: Make flags mutually exclusive or define one explicit mode enum; record enabled rule IDs and refuse zero-rule scans.
findings.validation: CHECK-073 evaluates the exact guards.

findings.title: Scanner dependency and test classification miss ordinary production cases
findings.finding: ImportedSymbol drops relative depth and dependency rule resolves only module, ignoring imported name and relative flag; from..import infrastructure therefore has an empty resolution key. Any filename containing test, including latest.py, is classified as test and exempted from architecture/assert checks. source_roots configuration is unused in package mapping.
findings.recommended_action: Resolve imports relative to actual packages/source roots, preserve depth and imported submodules, and use precise test patterns/explicit inventory rather than substring exemptions.
findings.validation: CHECK-074/076 demonstrate both false-negative paths.

findings.title: Noqa recognition treats string contents as suppression directives
findings.finding: Both suppression helpers regex-match raw lines without tokenizing comments. A production assert with message containing # noqa suppresses itself despite no actual comment. Policy exceptions therefore arise accidentally from string data.
findings.recommended_action: Use tokenize comment tokens with declared line scope and record every suppression in the receipt; fail malformed codes rather than dropping them.
findings.validation: CHECK-075 uses an in-memory assert with a literal message.

findings.title: Test runner does not propagate all failed prerequisites
findings.finding: Collection, mechanical gate and focused tests always execute in sequence regardless of earlier failure. Malformed gate stdout at exit0 creates GATE_ERROR but still labels gatePASS; final exit ignores collection failure. Subprocesses have no timeout and receipt discards raw outputs and exact argv, limiting replay/custody.
findings.recommended_action: Stop or explicitly isolate dependent execution after failed prerequisites, make parse/schema/findings failures fail closed, include collection in aggregate status and bind exact argv/full outputs/source/config with bounded timeouts.
findings.validation: CHECK-078 reproduces status logic on synthetic values without subprocess execution.

findings.title: Quality gate can pass unavailable targets and ineffective raises restrictions
findings.finding: File discovery silently ignores missing paths and pytest node IDs, yielding zero-file success. A match=None AST node is accepted as a match restriction. Presence of dead/nested assertions or arbitrary raises-named calls also satisfies no-assertion checks, which is consistent only with the stated narrow syntactic ceiling.
findings.recommended_action: Refuse unresolved/zero required populations and either resolve pytest selectors to files or accept explicit paths only. Validate effective match values and keep behavioral adequacy separate.
findings.validation: CHECK-077 demonstrates None bypass; other limits follow full body review.

findings.title: Scanner documentation promises a larger active rule set and stricter exit than supplied
findings.finding: Default registry contains24 AST rule classes plus three architecture rules; ViewDoesNotImportOrmRule exists but is not registered. README says findings imply nonzero exit, but controller returns0 for warning-only results. Several50-item rubric checks are not implemented and clean scan is not comprehensive review.
findings.recommended_action: Publish the exact active predicate inventory and severity exit policy, register/test intended missing rules, and retain README no-proof ceiling.
findings.validation: CHECK-079 records actual24 names; source inspection establishes registration/exit behavior.

findings.title: Commit/reveal snippet treats unavailable or empty population as success
findings.finding: Verification runs only if the manifest exists, missing cases defaults to an empty list, and comparisons use assert. Missing evidence therefore produces no refusal and optimized Python removes hash comparisons; no timestamp/precommitment or blinding follows from digest equality alone.
findings.recommended_action: Require explicit nonempty exact case inventory, strict manifest shape/duplicates/path rules and unconditional mismatch errors; retain old commitment versions and independent chronology.
findings.validation: CHECK-086; source review of assertion and defaults.

findings.title: Paper extraction omits mathematical content from claim-statement bindings
findings.finding: Display-math branches continue before appending to an active claim buffer, so changing a displayed equation can leave claim statement hash/UUID unchanged. Claim-header lines also continue before inline extraction; numeric inline formulas are excluded and embedded display dollars are additionally parsed as inline. Exhaustive typed inventory is not achieved.
findings.recommended_action: Use one explicit grammar with disjoint formula spans; bind claim raw spans including displayed equations and preserve title/type/occurrences. Report rejected/unclosed syntax and extraction coverage rather than exhaustive labels.
findings.validation: CHECK-081/082 show duplicate classification, numeric exclusion and unchanged statement despite changed equation.

findings.title: Byte anchors describe newline-normalized text instead of source bytes
findings.finding: Markdown and TeX use read_text with universal newline conversion, then re-encode normalized strings to compute offsets. On CRLF files every preceding line shifts byte positions; location hashes contain no raw file digest to resolve representation ambiguity. Existing tests only check nonempty ranges.
findings.recommended_action: Read raw bytes, define decoding/newline representation explicitly, compute anchors against that representation and include raw source digest; test exact slicing with CRLF and Unicode.
findings.validation: CHECK-080 demonstrates reported2 versus actual3 for second-line start.

findings.title: ZIP checksum cross-check verifies names and can pass without bound modules
findings.finding: Digest columns in SHA256SUMS/MANIFEST are ignored; arbitrary suffix matches satisfy required names without unique rooted members or byte checks. Ancillary checksum/document requirements make required nonempty even when code/proof bindings are absent, bypassing advertised no-bindings refusal. Whole ZIP hash is useful custody but does not repair these missing checks.
findings.recommended_action: Separate binding presence from ancillary membership; validate digest syntax and each exact uniquely rooted regular member against expected bytes, reject duplicates/ambiguous paths, and name membership-only receipts accurately.
findings.validation: CHECK-083/084; existing source test accepts abc12345/def67890 as checksum columns.

findings.title: Paper coverage links are unverified ledger associations
findings.finding: Ledger entries become code/Lean bindings without file existence/hash/declaration/type checks; fallback number matching can associate a different claim kind. Regex Lean declaration names and inherited formula bindings are counted as coverage. Test fixture uses a True theorem and a pass function, so coverage is association coverage, not proof/implementation adequacy.
findings.recommended_action: Rename fields to association coverage or validate exact source/statement/premise bindings separately; preserve missing/ambiguous references and never infer proof from a path/name.
findings.validation: Full source inspection; no Lean/runtime replay or theorem correspondence claim.

findings.title: Identity CONSISTENT conflates missing metadata with verified parity
findings.finding: Missing author/version/date/PDF produces no mismatch; creator/author checks merely contain Carroll and PDF author flag is not enforced. Different full author names can pass, and fallback version1.0.0 is synthesized. Pydantic shape bounds do not enforce count/hash/key/reference consistency.
findings.recommended_action: Use explicit unavailable/partial/consistent/mismatch states, compare declared complete identities and validate manifest relationships/digests independently.
findings.validation: CHECK-085 covers all-missing identity case; model invariants inspected in full.

findings.title: Strict Boolean recipe rejects every Boolean
findings.finding: isinstance(v,bool) and not isinstance(v,(int,str)) rejects True and False since bool subclasses int. This normative recipe cannot admit any valid Boolean record.
findings.recommended_action: Use type(v) is bool or isinstance(v,bool) and test both valid Booleans plus integers/strings; use explicit exceptions rather than assert for production.
findings.validation: CHECK-087 evaluates all relevant finite examples.

findings.title: Skill root path recipe has an off-by-one parent index
findings.finding: The stated .agents/skills/name/scripts/file.py hierarchy has repository root at file.parents[4]; parents[3] is .agents. The os.path dirname plus four ascents alternative is correct, so the supposedly equivalent recipes disagree.
findings.recommended_action: Use script-relative verified root resolution and test the actual installed hierarchy; do not mix dirname ascent count with Path.parents index.
findings.validation: CHECK-088 gives exact paths.

findings.title: Cochain dimension and coordinate bounds need explicit representative restrictions
findings.finding: For a3-cycle without2-faces every standard edge is closed and has quotient l1 distance1. These raw surviving cochains span dimension3, but beta1=1; equality applies to quotient classes or chosen complementary representatives. Positive observer weights and quotient descent likewise do not bound arbitrary raw gauge coordinates: d0=[-1,1], c=cprime=100 has quotient norm0.
findings.recommended_action: State whether survivors are classes, harmonic/optimal residuals or raw cochains. Require norm-bounded representative and actual per-observer descent before using coordinate inequality; keep quotient and representative norms distinct.
findings.validation: CHECK-089 gives primal/dual witnesses and ranks; CHECK-090 gives exact coordinate counterexample.

findings.title: Trace-distance product formula omits real normalized domain
findings.finding: The product one-half norm(a-b) norm(a+b) computes rank-one trace distance for normalized real vectors. It fails for allowed-looking complex unit vectors a=1,b=i: both densities are[1] yet product1. Unnormalized vectors also need scale treatment.
findings.recommended_action: Declare real unit-sphere domain or use phase-invariant complex formula with normalization/zero checks; distinguish lift fibers from signed cochain orientation.
findings.validation: CHECK-091 records exact unit-phase counterexample.

findings.title: Dual flow statement reverses complementary slackness and closure statement is overbroad
findings.finding: Source says nonzero edge flow requires zero residual. In weighted l1 duality nonzero residual requires y=w*sign(r), while zero residual permits any bounded feasible dual coordinate. Source also says norms cannot determine closure; a correctly computed definite exact norm(d1r)=0 is exactly closure, although norm(r) alone cannot determine exactness and unbound scalar claims are not certificates.
findings.recommended_action: Correct signed saturation/free-zero-coordinate conditions and distinguish actual computed exact norm from an unverified scalar or seminorm. Preserve actual operators/certificates in receipts.
findings.validation: CHECK-092 exhibits primal=dual=1 with nonzero r,y; CHECK-093 states exact norm equivalence.

findings.title: Encoding repair policy identifies valid mathematical Unicode as corruption
findings.finding: Documentation manager lists valid Phi, lambda, arrows and middle dots as mojibake and mandates automatic repair; lint policy additionally standardizes to dollar delimiters then says to flag/replace those same delimiters. These instructions can rewrite sound mathematical source without evidence of corruption.
findings.recommended_action: Require byte/decoding diagnosis and explicit before/after provenance; preserve valid Unicode and state one noncontradictory supported delimiter grammar.
findings.validation: Full source-body comparison; no source rewritten.

findings.title: Rule corpus contains mutually conflicting canonical contracts
findings.finding: Same architecture rule forbids reexports then requires public __all__ reexports; triad manager manifests are mandated while persona manifests are permanently retired; exact rational JSON is p/q-only in one rule but unit denominators must omit slash in another. Historical and scoped exceptions need explicit precedence to avoid incompatible gates. Publication rules additionally require and retire claim ledgers/maps, require and prohibit AuthorityEffect in manuscripts, and both mandate dated ZIP names and ban calendar dates in deliverables.
findings.recommended_action: Version and scope rules by current owner/profile; retain historical definitions as historical and make policy conflict an explicit refusal rather than automatic source mutation.
findings.validation: Full text comparison; related F052 policy conflicts preserved.

findings.title: Absent constructive instance is incorrectly equated with uninhabitability
findings.finding: A rule says an axiom set without an exhibited constructive inhabitant is an uninstantiable specification. Absence of an exhibited instance is absence of positive evidence, not proof that no instance exists. Requiring an instance for promotion is a defensible policy, with a different logical claim.
findings.recommended_action: Label instance status unestablished/unavailable, reserve inconsistent or uninhabitable for a proof, and distinguish by-construction subtype theorems from external adequacy.
findings.validation: Direct logical distinction; no external formal library replay.

findings.title: Set-plus-count exhaustion predicate assumes unique identifiers
findings.finding: Equal sets and equal list lengths can pass when duplicate multiplicities differ: declared[a,a,b] and checked[a,b,b]. Exact inventory/candidate binding requires unique IDs or multiset agreement, not counts and sets alone.
findings.recommended_action: Validate unique identifiers at ingress or compare canonical multisets while binding each checked result to candidate bytes.
findings.validation: CHECK-094; bounded predicate issue, not a claim current owners admit duplicate IDs.

findings.title: Rational squared lengths do not force every deficit to be irrational
findings.finding: Mathematical hygiene says rational positive squared edge lengths yield transcendental angles/deficits and delta notin Q. A flat Euclidean triangulated square fan has squared lengths1,2 and deficit0. Nonzero angle/deficit hypotheses cannot be omitted.
findings.recommended_action: State the precise nonzero algebraic-exponential hypotheses and allow exactly flat rational-zero deficits; retain interval exclusions only for claimed nonzero curvature.
findings.validation: CHECK-096 exact flat fan construction.

findings.title: Epsilon-set ranking differs from strict primary priority in the same rule
findings.finding: The global epsilon policy first admits candidates within epsilon of minimal discrete score, then selects near-minimal Xi, so it may choose a strictly worse primary score. This conflicts with the nearby strict lexicographic priority requirement even though it avoids pairwise tolerance cycles.
findings.recommended_action: Declare two distinct policies with explicit selection contract or apply exact lexicographic ordering; bind policy/epsilon into receipts and tests.
findings.validation: CHECK-095 selects B(primary1/2,Xi0) over A(primary0,Xi100) at epsilon1.

findings.title: Finite-QM workflow imports APIs absent from current bridge owner
findings.finding: The workflow imports evaluate_state_observables, verify_exact_state_with_engine, evaluate_state_fidelity and evaluate_bures_geometry from engine_bridge; its Born/Gleason and tomography bridge helpers are also absent from the complete current module. Present APIs supply exact-to-diagnostic conversion and interval enclosures, not the documented bidirectional workflow. Existing quantum review distinguishes actual finite tomography from physical/Born selection.
findings.recommended_action: Update examples to actual owning APIs and declare one-way conversion; bind any restoration/migration to exact source and bounded tests. Preserve earlier recipes as history rather than claim current executability.
findings.validation: CHECK-097 plus full156-line owner inspection and pinned prior QP-C027/context; no compilation.

findings.title: Mutation equivalence guidance promotes small-case enumeration beyond its carrier
findings.finding: The custody skill says prove equivalence by exhaustive search over small cases. This proves only that finite population unless it exhausts the admitted domain or a reduction theorem connects all cases. Two integer functions can agree on0..100 and differ at101.
findings.recommended_action: State the complete finite domain or supply a mathematical reduction/universal proof; otherwise label mutant apparently equivalent on tested cases and keep unchecked remainder.
findings.validation: CHECK-098 supplies bounded-versus-unbounded counterexample.

findings.title: Paper zero-curvature preflight requires stronger exactness than claimed
findings.finding: The preflight requires both Phi1=0 and Gamma2=0 for papers asserting zero curvature. Closed nonexact cochains have Gamma2=0 and Phi1>0, so a valid zero-curvature claim would be refused by this declared rule. Exact repair and closedness are different obligations.
findings.recommended_action: Select certificates for the actual claim: closure d1omega=0 versus exactness omega in image(d0), and require valid dual/primal checks only for declared optimization statements.
findings.validation: Existing CHECK-089 supplies exact3-cycle witnesses Phi1=1,Gamma2=0; this is rule inconsistency, not an executed preflight failure.

findings.title: Artifact custody advice improperly upgrades declarations and frequent conventions into laws
findings.finding: Custody skill says artifact epistemic declarations outrank plans and self-rules should be enforced biconditionally by default; it also calls98percent conventions undocumented invariants. A source declaration can be wrong, one-way implication cannot be silently reversed, and frequency does not establish normative scope. Its later advice that verdicts require recomputation correctly limits the earlier rhetoric.
findings.recommended_action: Preserve declarations as source claims, resolve ownership/version and actual checks independently, and never strengthen logical direction or infer universal rules from frequencies.
findings.validation: Full-body logical review; no source/corpus mutation or claim that the specific historical examples are false.

findings.title: Sprint lifecycle declarations conflict and require their own future outputs
findings.finding: Retrospective pre-gate requires retrospective and VP briefing artifacts before retrospective; VP briefing requires its own briefing before evaluation. Planning supplies three documents but review demands eight including future completion/retro. Evidence roots disagree across manager/review/execution, commitment is soft in538 but hard in541, and deprecated improve-autoskill still has a required hash. No single literal first-run state machine can satisfy all these requirements without undefined placeholders/precedence.
findings.recommended_action: Choose one versioned artifact/state contract, distinct creation/completion states and canonical roots; migrate historical recipes explicitly and test first-run, exception and cleanup transitions.
findings.validation: CHECK-101 finite prerequisite cycle plus complete cross-file review. Actual hosts may implement different precedence; no orchestrator run.

findings.title: Sprint parsing loses or rejects supported cleanup identities
findings.finding: Both planning and review derive sprint_number using branch.split("-")[1], so sprint-108-0 becomes108 and targets the parent sprint. Explicit108-0 instead reaches int(sprint_number), which raises ValueError. The advertised cleanup hierarchy is therefore not represented by these examples.
findings.recommended_action: Treat sprint identity as an opaque validated string; preserve the entire suffix, and use a separately declared numeric database key when required.
findings.validation: CHECK-099 reproduces both exact expressions without invoking workflow.

findings.title: Displayed hard gates can accept empty evidence or return successful shell status after refusal
findings.finding: Planning artifact gate uses test-f only and merely echoes HARD BLOCK on failure, without exit1; its branch ends in successful echo. Review also uses existence rather than content despite a later all-documents-have-content condition. Completion predicate accepts any text containing two section names, including a zero-story zero-result document. Other manual instructions are stronger, so the snippets do not implement the claimed composite gate.
findings.recommended_action: Implement explicit nonzero refusal, typed required nonempty artifacts, source/task/result binding and unknown/error branches. Keep presence, structural and executed-verification states distinct.
findings.validation: CHECK-100 demonstrates exact header predicate; shell exit behavior follows the displayed echo-only branch, no shell execution claimed.

findings.title: Web-edit audit compares sprint branch to itself and cannot establish UI origin
findings.finding: The recipe selects sprint-{N}..HEAD. On that sprint branch at its own tip this is empty, omitting every sprint commit. Noreply author and at-most-two files identify neither GitHub UI origin nor bypassed CI; comment mentions no GPG signature but code never checks one. Recursive VETO grep similarly counts mentions rather than distinct events.
findings.recommended_action: Bind a recorded sprint base and reviewed head; inspect provider event/CI metadata if UI origin matters, otherwise label only the heuristic. Count structured event IDs rather than text mentions.
findings.validation: CHECK-102 exact revision-reachability model; no network or Git mutation/replay.

findings.title: Garden/count pairs do not diagnose or detect all colour drift
findings.finding: The census skill says pairing operation count with substitution count identifies size change versus colour drift. Distinct colour assignments can have equal operation/substitution counts: A:X→X,B:Y→Y admits AA and BB; A:X→X,B:X→Y admits AA and BA. Both counts are(2,2) while the wiring relation changes. Even when counts move they do not uniquely identify cause.
findings.recommended_action: Bind full operation identities/colours and the composable relation or its canonical source digest; use counts as diagnostics and preserve valid exact fixture/population assertions.
findings.validation: CHECK-103 enumerates all four unary pairs in each2-operation garden.

findings.title: Uncalled-module limitations incorrectly claim dynamic imports only under-report
findings.finding: The skill correctly admits stem/dynamic-import limitations, then says both failure modes are toward silence. A static test import plus a production importlib.import_module call produces test-only static importers although production is wired: an over-report. Static graph absence cannot establish runtime unreachability.
findings.recommended_action: Describe both false-positive and false-negative modes; require caller/entrypoint/plugin review before declaring a module unwired, and distinguish static references from actual reachable execution.
findings.validation: CHECK-104 parses complete independent code strings only; external operations owner not rerun.

findings.title: Missing declared falsifier does not imply unfalsifiable acceptance criterion
findings.finding: The gate auditor says every implementation satisfies a criterion naming no falsifier. Build success or a test predicate can fail without a separately written Decisive mutation field; a syntax mutation is an immediate counterexample. The later diagnostic-only count disclaimer is correct but does not justify the earlier equivalence.
findings.recommended_action: Report missing explicit falsification documentation separately from actual falsifiability and semantic adequacy; inspect/test the real predicate before saying nothing can turn it red.
findings.validation: CHECK-105 parses valid/invalid Python source to show a concrete falsifier without a named declaration.

findings.title: Publication language sweeps cannot certify total mathematical honesty
findings.finding: Anti-DIME bans proves and mathematical/common terms such as Primal Dual and Quarantine, while its own verdict guarantees100percent verified/honest materials. Generic wording controls can reject valid mathematical statements and still miss false claims. Public-claim statuses also overlap: a fully proved Lean implication under explicit analytic hypotheses is both MECHANIZED and HYP_GATED unless precedence is declared.
findings.recommended_action: Separate mathematical result status, premise scope, editorial style and publication authorization; declare status precedence or independent axes. Emit scoped reviewed findings rather than100percent truth certification and narrow lexical bans by context.
findings.validation: Full-body logical review; no external source, publication or Lean replay.
